answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the zephyr hash is checked against the sparrow checkpoint at intake, the garden audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 320 aliases cost 121 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
